basics.name: Supplier catalogues as a vocabulary source: McMaster-Carr, MISUMI and igus (plus the 2017 McMaster-Carr print catalogue scanned on the Internet Archive)
basics.url: McMaster-Carr: https://www.mcmaster.com/ (example category URL opened: https://www.mcmaster.com/products/torque-limiters/); McMaster-Carr Catalog 123 (2017) full scan: https://archive.org/details/mcmastercarr123; MISUMI Americas: https://www.misumi.com/ and its engineering blog https://blog.misumiusa.com/ (the e-catalogue itself, us.misumi-ec.com, refused automated access, so no catalogue page could be opened); igus: https://www.igus.com/ (e.g. https://www.igus.com/custom-parts-services/3d-printing/3d-printed-gear) and its Engineer's Toolbox https://toolbox.igus.com/category/design-guides
basics.resource_type: Supplier catalogue (three online industrial parts catalogues, used here as a naming/vocabulary reference rather than as a shop), plus one scanned print catalogue on the Internet Archive
basics.cost: Free to browse. The parts themselves are paid. McMaster-Carr sells mainly to businesses (Wikipedia calls it business-to-business) but browsing and CAD downloads are free; MISUMI and igus catalogues and CAD are free, some igus/MISUMI tools ask for a free account [uncertain]
basics.license: All rights reserved for all three (commercial catalogues; igus footer reads '(c) igus, 2026'). Linking to category pages is fine; copying text, drawings or photos is not. McMaster's page carries a 'noindex, noarchive, noimageindex' robots tag, a sign it does not want its content copied or archived. The Internet Archive scan of McMaster Catalog 123 has no licence or rights statement in its metadata, so treat it as copyright McMaster-Carr: link only [uncertain]
basics.language: English (McMaster-Carr is US English and inch-first with metric ranges; MISUMI and igus run many country sites in other languages, e.g. MISUMI Japan/Germany/India and igus Germany/UK, but only the English sites were checked)
basics.year: McMaster-Carr founded 1901, first printed catalogue 1908 (506 pages), catalogue issued yearly (Wikipedia); the scanned Catalog 123 is from 2017 (about 3,870 pages); website live and current in 2026. MISUMI blog posts cited date from 2014-2015 and the blog is updated to September 2026. igus site '(c) igus, 2026', Engineer's Toolbox posts current in 2026. MISUMI and igus founding years not checked [uncertain]
basics.access_barrier: For a person in a normal browser: none (free browsing, no login needed to view categories, though McMaster's site needs JavaScript; its plain HTML only shows the 26 top-level department names and 'Our website requires JavaScript'). For automated tools: high. McMaster served a 'To continue browsing, please log in' wall to a scripted browser, and MISUMI's e-catalogue (us/uk/de/in/jp.misumi-ec.com) returned Akamai 'Access Denied' to every scripted request. igus pages load normally
basics.image_license: All rights reserved (the clean grey McMaster line drawings and photos, MISUMI and igus product renders and CAD). Useful to look at and link to, not to copy. CAD downloads are licensed for designing with the vendor's parts, not for republishing [uncertain]
basics.authority_level: Manufacturer / distributor. Very reliable for the trade names, variants and specs of off-the-shelf parts; not neutral (each names things its own way, e.g. McMaster's 'instant-bonding adhesives' for cyanoacrylate glue, igus's brand names like iglide/iglidur, drylin, igubal)

coverage.covers: McMaster-Carr: about 595,000-700,000 products (site meta text says 'over 595,000'; a 2022 blog says 700,000) in 26 departments (Fastening & Joining, Hardware, Power Transmission, Material Handling, Electrical & Lighting, and so on). Among the standard hardware sit many clever-mechanism families, each with a named category and variants: torque limiters (friction type, double-spring type, with matching sprockets), adjustable-torque threaded knobs that slip at a set torque, one-way locking needle-roller bearing clutches (drawn-cup roller clutches), spring plungers and retractable spring plungers (index/detent pins), push-button and expanding-diameter quick-release pins, toggle clamps (hold-down, push/pull, right-angle, squeeze-action plier, auto-adjusting), draw latches, cam latches, tight-hold latches, push-to-close and push-to-open latches, slide-bolt latches, position/lever-lock/friction/incremental-angle hinges, lift-off and soft-close hinges, detent turntables, gas springs (including remote-release), constant-force springs and retractors, rotary and linear speed limiters (dampers), linear solenoids, electromagnets and electromagnetic door and gate locks, gearmotors and speed reducers, bayonet/turn-lock connectors, and adhesives by type. MISUMI: a configurable-parts catalogue for factory automation (search results cite over 3.8 million products [uncertain]) with categories such as indexing plungers, spring plungers, clutches and brakes, couplings (including torque-limiting couplings) and magnetic transmission drives, plus the free 'inCAD Library' of 200-300+ complete example mechanisms (aligning, escapement, clamping, grip, lifting, feeding mechanisms) with downloadable CAD. igus: plastic motion parts: plain and self-aligning bearings (clip bearings, clevis joints, rod ends, spherical balls, 'variable double joint'), drylin linear slides, dryspin lead screws, gears (spur, bevel, racks, right-angle gearbox), modular strain-wave gears, modular worm gears, worm gear joints, planetary gear, slewing rings, cable carriers (e-chain, e-spool, e-loop, zig-zag), robot joints, and 3D-printing filament/SLS powder for wear parts
coverage.organisation: McMaster-Carr: department -> product family -> picture-tile subcategories -> filter panel with small schematic drawings -> part table; each family often opens with an 'About ...' explainer box (the 2017 catalogue has about 170 'About' boxes, e.g. 'About Spring Plungers', 'About Position, Lever-Lock, and Friction Hinges', 'About Adhesives and Sealants'). Works surprisingly well for someone who doesn't know the terms, because you can browse by picture and read the explainer (the Ben Edelstein article calls it 'an engineer's handbook and catalog in one' and describes using the subcategory descriptions to decide which lock washer to buy). Search accepts plain words. MISUMI: deep numbered category tree (e.g. category codes like M03... for locating parts, M09... for clutches & brakes seen in search results [uncertain]) with spec filters and a part-number configurator; aimed at people who already know the part type. igus: organised by its own product lines and brand names (e-chain, iglide, drylin, igubal, xiros, dryspin), then by generic type, which is hard going for beginners who don't know the brand names
coverage.scope_match: medium: the catalogues are mostly standard hardware (out of scope), but their clever-mechanism families (torque limiters, index/spring plungers, toggle clamps, latches, one-way clutches, position hinges, gas springs, solenoids, electromagnetic locks, strain-wave and worm gear joints, adhesives by type) give the correct trade names and variant lists for many in-scope entries
coverage.taxonomy_used: Commercial, by product family and then by feature/spec, not by motion or function. McMaster-Carr: 26 top-level departments (Abrading & Polishing; Building & Grounds; Electrical & Lighting; Fabricating; Fastening & Joining; Filtering; Flow & Level Control; Furniture & Storage; Hand Tools; Hardware; Heating & Cooling; Lubricating; Material Handling; Measuring & Inspecting; Office Supplies & Signs; Pipe, Tubing, Hose & Fittings; Plumbing and Janitorial; Power Transmission; Pressure & Temperature Control; Pulling & Lifting; Raw Materials; Safety Supplies; Sawing & Cutting; Sealing; Shipping; Suspending). Within a family, subcategories name variants by how they work (e.g. 'push-button' vs 'expanding-diameter' quick-release pins; 'friction' vs 'double-spring' torque limiters; 'incremental-angle' vs 'set-angle' position hinges). MISUMI: mechanical components tree by function (linear motion, rotary motion, locating/positioning, etc. [uncertain]). igus: product-line taxonomy (cable carriers; bearings/rollers/slewing rings; linear bearings, actuators and motors; lead screws; gears and modular gearboxes; automation and robotics; custom parts/3D printing; bar stock)
coverage.example_types: torque limiter (friction torque limiter, double-spring torque limiter, ball-detent torque limiter); adjustable-torque threaded knob (slips at a set torque); torque-limiting coupling; magnetic transmission drive (non-contact magnetic gear that skips poles when overloaded, MISUMI TM series); one-way locking needle-roller bearing clutch (drawn-cup roller clutch); spring plunger (ball-nose, long-nose) used as a detent catch; retractable/indexing plunger (pull-ring, L-handle, with or without locking/rest position); push-button quick-release pin and expanding-diameter quick-release pin; toggle clamp (hold-down, push/pull, right-angle, squeeze-action plier, auto-adjusting); draw latch (snap-down, turn-to-open, tight-hold); cam latch and lift-and-turn cam latch; push-to-close and push-to-open latch; position hinge, lever-lock hinge, friction hinge and incremental-angle position hinge; detent turntable (one-, four- and eight-position); remote-release gas spring; constant-force spring and constant-force retractor; rotary and linear speed limiter (damper); linear solenoid (push/pull); electromagnetic door and gate lock (magnetic lock); surface-contact electromagnet; strain-wave gear and modular worm gear joint (igus); planetary gear and right-angle gearbox; turn-lock / twist-lock (bayonet) connector; instant-bonding adhesive (cyanoacrylate), two-part epoxy, contact adhesive, hot-melt adhesive, threadlocker and retaining compound
coverage.making_methods: General engineering, machine building and factory automation (all three); robotics (igus robot joints and strain-wave/worm gearboxes, MISUMI automation); 3D printing (igus sells wear-resistant 3D-printing filament and a 3D-printed gear service with an online gear configurator; McMaster and MISUMI CAD models are handy for designing around bought parts); woodwork/DIY only incidentally (hinges, latches, adhesives)
coverage.item_count: McMaster-Carr: 'over 595,000 products' (site description); 2017 print catalogue about 3,870 pages with about 170 'About ...' explainer boxes. MISUMI: over 3.8 million products [uncertain]; inCAD Library 300+ application examples when launched in 2015, reportedly about 200 now [uncertain]. igus: not stated on pages opened [uncertain]
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: torque-limiting: yes (McMaster friction and double-spring torque limiters, adjustable-torque knobs that 'disengage and turn freely'; MISUMI torque-limiting couplings and the magnetic drive that slips). self-locking: partial (igus article on self-locking lead screws; McMaster lever-lock hinges, tight-hold latches). hand-release only: yes (quick-release pins, indexing plungers, toggle clamps, cam and draw latches). one-way/ratchet: yes (one-way locking needle-roller clutches, 'with ratchet lock' variants, ratchet crank handles). indexing/detent: yes (spring plungers 'for positioning, locking, indexing, and ejecting', detent turntables, incremental-angle position hinges, indexing plungers). over-centre: yes in practice (toggle clamps, draw latches), though the catalogues rarely use the word 'over-centre' [uncertain]. compliant: little (vibration-damping mounts, flexible couplings only). print-in-place: no. gear trains/gearboxes: yes (McMaster gearmotors, speed reducers, planetary reducers; igus strain-wave gears, worm gear joints, planetary gear, 3D-printed gears). powered connectors: yes (McMaster linear solenoids, electromagnets, electromagnetic door and gate locks, electronic-lock latches; MISUMI solenoid-related parts [uncertain]). adhesive types: yes, strongly in McMaster, which splits adhesives into high-strength (epoxies, acrylics, urethanes), instant-bonding (super glue/cyanoacrylate), contact, aerosol, hot-melt, pipe cement (PVC/CPVC solvent cement), threadlockers and retaining compounds, with an 'Adhesives Bonding Guide' matrix of which type suits metal, plastic, hard-to-bond plastics (polyethylene, polypropylene, PTFE), rubber, fibreglass, ceramic and glass, masonry, wood and fabric/paper
coverage.entry_structure: McMaster: family name, picture tiles, one- or two-paragraph 'About' explainer with small schematic drawings, spec filters, a part table (sizes, load/torque ratings, materials), and a downloadable 2D/3D CAD model per part. MISUMI: product page with spec table, configurable part number, CAD download, catalogue PDF page; inCAD Library entries show a whole mechanism with purpose, how it works and a bill of materials plus CAD [uncertain]. igus: product-line page with benefits, material recommendations, test data, application stories and links to configurators and service-life calculators
coverage.audience_level: professional (mechanical and manufacturing engineers, machine builders, maintenance staff); usable by hobbyists, and McMaster's explainers are readable by beginners

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: McMaster's picture tiles, plain one-line variant names and 'About' boxes make it the most beginner-friendly of the three, but everything is written as buying specs, not 'which one should I use'; MISUMI assumes you already know the part name; igus hides generic names behind brand names (iglide, drylin, igubal, e-chain)
usefulness.has_images: yes: McMaster uses consistent grey line drawings and photos (very clear, and deliberately plain); MISUMI and igus use product renders and photos; all three offer CAD models
usefulness.has_animations: mostly no. Some product videos (igus YouTube, MISUMI blog videos such as a reciprocating linear transfer demo); McMaster pages are static by design. CAD models can be rotated in McMaster's and MISUMI's viewers [uncertain]
usefulness.gaps: No 'how it works' animations or motion diagrams; no comparisons across families (e.g. torque limiter vs slip clutch vs shear pin); nothing on making the mechanism yourself (3D printing, print-in-place, compliant versions); brand/trade names instead of neutral terms in places; inch-first sizes (McMaster); heavy scripting and bot-blocking make them hard to cite or scrape; MISUMI's catalogue refused automated access entirely; content changes over time and old category URLs may move
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: Yes for McMaster: stable, readable family URLs of the form https://www.mcmaster.com/products/<family-name>/ (e.g. https://www.mcmaster.com/products/torque-limiters/), good as a 'buy one / see the variants' link from an encyclopedia entry, but they need JavaScript and may show a login wall to bots. MISUMI category and product URLs are long numeric codes (vona2/mech/M03.../ and vona2/detail/<id>/) and could not be opened here [uncertain]. igus product-line URLs are readable and stable (e.g. https://www.igus.com/custom-parts-services/3d-printing/3d-printed-gear)
usefulness.reusable_data: not reusable for the list itself: all rights reserved, and McMaster sets noindex/noarchive. McMaster links an 'API' in its footer, but it is an ordering integration for customers, not an open data set [uncertain]. The family NAMES (vocabulary) can be used freely as terms, since words and short names are not copyrightable, but the explainer text, drawings and CAD should be linked, not copied. The 2017 McMaster catalogue OCR text on the Internet Archive is searchable, which is how this entry's category names were checked
usefulness.maintained: Yes, all three are actively maintained commercial sites (McMaster Wikipedia page edited September 2026, igus '(c) 2026' with 2026 posts, MISUMI blog posts to September 2026). Old print catalogues survive on the Internet Archive (McMaster Catalog 123, 2017, uploaded 2023, about 39,000 views). The Wayback Machine could not be reached from this environment to check archived catalogue pages [uncertain]
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: 1) McMaster's 'About ...' box at the top of each family: a short plain explanation plus one simple drawing before any list; copy that pattern for each encyclopedia family. 2) Name variants by how they behave ('push-button', 'expanding-diameter', 'incremental-angle', 'remote-release', 'adjustable-torque') so the name itself teaches. 3) Picture-tile navigation: let beginners pick by look, not by term. 4) Filters with tiny schematic drawings (e.g. a drawing that shows what 'offset' means for a latch). 5) McMaster's Adhesives Bonding Guide matrix (adhesive type x material to bond, rated excellent/good) is a ready-made template for the adhesive part of the flow chart. 6) MISUMI's inCAD Library idea: show each component inside a small working example mechanism. 7) igus-style 'how long will it last' calculators and a gear configurator as optional links for printed gears. 8) A 'buy it' link per entry pointing at the McMaster family page, so makers can learn the trade name to search for
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes, as ratings rather than rules: torque ratings and bore sizes for torque limiters, holding force for toggle clamps and latches, spring end forces for plungers, force ratings for gas springs, pull force for electromagnets, stroke and force for solenoids, gear module/teeth ranges (igus spur gears module 0.5-3, 12-150 teeth; bevel gear ratio 1.1-1.5), igus test data (a laser-sintered iglide i3 gear lasted about five times as long as a machined POM gear in a gear-on-rack test). Adhesive bonding suitability by material (McMaster). Few general design rules (clearances, fits) for making your own
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: Yes, but for the vendors' own parts: McMaster downloadable CAD for nearly every part plus a SolidWorks add-in; MISUMI configurable part numbers (set dimensions) with CAD, and inCAD Components add-in for CAD [uncertain]; igus online gear configurator ('create a gear model with individual dimensions in less than 60 seconds'), service-life calculator and CAD configurators for 3D-printed wear parts
usefulness.file_formats: CAD downloads (2D DXF/DWG and 3D STEP and native CAD formats [uncertain]), PDF catalogue pages and data sheets, STL for igus 3D-printing uploads [uncertain]; McMaster 2017 catalogue as PDF and OCR text on the Internet Archive
usefulness.terminology_value: High for proper trade names, variants and aliases (e.g. McMaster: 'Also known as drawn-cup roller clutches', 'Also known as super glues and cyanoacrylates' for instant-bonding adhesives, 'Also known as pipe cements'; MISUMI search results list aliases for indexing plungers such as detent pins, hand-retractable pins, spring-loaded pins and locating pins [uncertain]). Watch for vendor-specific wording and brand names (igus). US English only for McMaster; MISUMI and igus country sites could supply translations [uncertain]
usefulness.decision_support: Faceted filters on every family (size, torque/force, material, mounting, actuation) with small explanatory drawings; McMaster 'A Guide to Choosing the Correct Gas Springs', 'About Push-to-Close Latches' (face-mount vs edge-mount by door offset) and the Adhesives Bonding Guide matrix; igus gear project checklist and service-life calculator. No cross-family selector (nothing asks 'what do you want to happen?')
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Original sources for their own ranges, but many clever parts are resold from specialist makers: MISUMI resells JW Winco/Ganter (GN-numbered) indexing plungers, so Ganter/JW Winco and Kipp catalogues overlap and may be the original naming source (JW Winco site checked, it lists technical guides such as 'Choosing the Correct Standard Part'). McMaster overlaps with Grainger and MSC (Wikipedia 'See also' also lists MISUMI USA). igus overlaps with other plastic bearing makers. The engineering blogs (MISUMI Mech Lab, igus Engineer's Toolbox) overlap with the textbooks already in this list
